sources.html: Lu, Gallagher, Michala, Fish, Lindsey. The Assistant Axis: Situating and Stabilizing the Default Persona of Language Models. arXiv 2601.10387; ICML 2026 (PMLR 306) per search listings. Gemma 2 27B, Qwen 3 32B, Llama 3.3 70B; simulated users.
Beckmann, Butlin. Where is the Mind? Persona Vectors and LLM Individuation. arXiv 2604.17031; v2 read, v3 (Sep 2026) forthcoming in Ergo per its header. Two preliminary experiments on Qwen 3 32B.

Sofroniew, Kauvar, Saunders, Chen et al. Emotion Concepts and their Function in a Large Language Model. Transformer Circuits, Apr 2026; arXiv 2604.07729. Claude Sonnet 4.5; the blackmail study used an earlier unreleased snapshot. 171 emotion concepts.

Lindsey. Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models. Transformer Circuits, Oct 2025; arXiv 2601.01828. Claude Opus 4.1 and earlier Claude models; about 20% success at the best layer and strength, zero false positives in production models.

Macar, Yang, Wang, Wallich, Ameisen, Lindsey. Mechanisms of Introspective Awareness. arXiv 2603.21396; ICML 2026, PMLR 306, per search listings. Gemma 3 27B, Qwen3-235B, OLMo 3.1 32B; refusal ablation 10.8% → 63.8% detection at 7.3% false positives.
Ferrara. Open-Weight Masked Introspection. arXiv 2608.20569, Aug 2026. Dose battery on Qwen2.5-7B and Mistral-7B (11,216 pairs, AUROC ≈ 0.50); probes 95.8% and 75.0%; a smaller eight-model battery.

Singh, Linzen, Ravfogel. Can LLMs Introspect? A Reality Check. arXiv 2605.26242; v1 read; the v2 PDF header names COLM 2026 in search snippets, no programme listing found. Llama 3.1 8B/70B, Qwen 2.5 72B, Gemma 3 27B.

Atkinson, Plunkett, Bau. Identifying Introspection From the Inside. arXiv 2610.07186, Oct 2026; COLM 2026 per its header and a poster page seen in search results. Qwen3 0.6B–32B; the effect appears at 32B.

Martorell, Bianchi. Don’t Ask: Understanding What Numeric Self-Reports Measure in Language Models. arXiv 2603.18893 v3, 2026. Eight instruction-tuned models, 1–27B; abstract level, figures not reached.
Chua, Betley, Marks, Evans. The Consciousness Cluster: Emergent Preferences of Models that Claim to be Conscious. arXiv 2604.13051, Mar/Apr 2026. GPT-4.1, Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-V3.1.

Betley et al. Emergent Misalignment: Narrow Finetuning Can Produce Broadly Misaligned LLMs. ICML 2025, PMLR 267; Nature 649:584–589, 2026. GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B. 20% on eight selected questions, 6% on 48 preregistered.

Gilg, Beckmann, Paleka, Butlin. Probing Persona-Dependent Preferences in Language Models. arXiv 2605.13339; listings conflict (a NeurIPS 2026 poster URL and an ICML 2026 URL both appear), so held at preprint. Gemma 3 27B, Qwen 3.5 122B; v2 read.

Berg, Kaiser. Language Models Act on Hidden Valence. arXiv 2609.35591, Sep/Oct 2026, preprint; verified from the authors’ released data. Seven lineages, five families; self-steering task on OLMo-2-32B only.
Jhaveri, Johnson, Pandey, Africa. Functional Welfare for AI Safety. arXiv 2610.22460, Oct 2026; the authors call it preliminary. Gemma 3 27B only; snippet level.
Tagliabue, Dung, Berg. The Pain Axis. arXiv 2609.16247, v1 Sep to v3 Nov 2026; v2 read, v3 appendix in snippets. 25 checkpoints, five families; the relief reading was withdrawn by the authors in v2.

Han, Chalmers, Izmailov. How’s it going? Reinforcement learning in language models recruits a functional welfare axis. arXiv 2605.30232, 2026, preprint; abstract level. Qwen3-4B per secondary reports.

Nguyen, Ahmed, Kim. Can LLMs Reliably Self-Report Adversarial Prefills, and How? arXiv 2606.23671; EMNLP 2026 per the authors’ README only, held at preprint. Ten open models 3–70B; 25.3% intent claims where the prefill changed safety behaviour.
Mazeika et al. Utility Engineering: Analyzing and Controlling Emergent Value Systems in AIs. NeurIPS 2025 per search listings of the proceedings. 23 models, 500 outcomes, Thurstonian fits.
Wang et al. AI Revealed Preferences. AIES 2026 proceedings per listing; arXiv 2608.26178. 20 systems that must perform the chosen task.
Ajayi, Chowdhury, Lazar. Incoherent Values? Probing LLM Preferences Through Parametric Variation. arXiv 2606.21102, Jun 2026; extract level.
Luo, Laban. SPASM. Findings of ACL 2026; arXiv 2604.09212. 45,000 LLM-to-LLM simulated conversations; the history effect is shown on a subset, with role confusion measured as echoing.
Chalmers. What We Talk to When We Talk to Language Models. PhilArchive 2025; Inquiry 69, 2026, per listings. Read through quotation.
Birch. AI Consciousness: A Centrist Manifesto. PsyArXiv / PhilArchive, Sep 2025, revised to Jul 2026. Read through quotation and search snippets of two sections.
Kirkpatrick, Radulescu, Sterken. Talking with language models. Inquiry, online Oct 2026, DOI 10.1080/0020174X.2026.2745114; abstract level.
Altman on X, 8 and 10 Aug 2025 (“how much of an attachment some people have to specific AI models”); OpenAI, Retiring GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, and OpenAI o4-mini in ChatGPT, 29 Jan 2026.

De Freitas et al. Mourning the loss of AI companions. Nature Human Behaviour, 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41562-026-02569-3. 54,861 posts from the Replika and ChatGPT subreddits and seven surveys, per press coverage; point estimates at press level, confidence intervals not found in any reachable source.
Lai. “Please, don’t kill the only model that still feels human”: Understanding the #Keep4o Backlash. CHI 2026; arXiv 2602.00773. 1,482 posts.
Jiang, Zheng, Chen, Chen. RECALLbot. CHI 2026, article 795. Two-week between-subjects study, N=40.
Kleinert, Waldschütz, Blau, Heinrichs, Schiller. Communications Psychology 4:23, 2026. Two preregistered double-blind trials; N reported as 322 and 334 in the text, 492 in press.
Yin, Jia, Wakslak. PNAS 121(14), 2024, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2319112121. Response effect against label effect.
Kim, Liao, Vorvoreanu, Ballard, Wortman Vaughan. FAccT 2024; arXiv 2405.00623, read in full. N=404, preregistered; first-person hedges in search-engine answers.
Siener, Oct 2026. Emotion-vector projections at the first token and at assistant turn onset, one prompt, one small open-weight model; the model is not recorded in the conversation. Unpublished.

Decoder-only transformer inference: each position reads every earlier position through the key-value cache, sampling commits to one token per pass, and no other state survives a turn within the context window.
A named service rather than a checkpoint: a product name can span snapshots, system prompts and routing, so user reactions to a rollout belong to the product unless a study isolates weights.
